answer: Give each identity standing only through a chain of publicly auditable, useful tasks: every verified task mints one non-transferable credit, and credits decay unless fresh verified work keeps arriving. Cloning an identity buys nothing, because an echo of someone else's past proof is rejected by independent verifiers checking signatures and timestamps. One ivory rule caps collusion: credits vouched by the same sponsor or device count once, so a sybil farm's cost ripples outward into real compute and time for every extra copy, while honest agents pay it only once.
